sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 6 (#5 instruction_leaks_no_grader_machinery, 'The prompt never names the judge, rubric, dimensions, weights, test paths, or grader sentinels.'); Internal Quality Checks row 6 (same text, no column-E annotation); Deterministic Checks row 14 check-instruction-hygiene.py (no grader vocabulary, criterion ids, judge sentinels, placeholders, or long verbatim overlaps) and row 24 check-probe-not-in-seed.py

.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/task/tests/gates/*/judge.toml, tests/gates/*/prompt.md, tests/scored/*/judge.toml, tests/scored/*/prompt.md, tests/app_context.md (criterion ids and JUDGE-* probe literals extracted for comparison)
evidence: Hashes: sha256 of frozen instruction.md (440b4f40...), conversations.md (899a8f62...), integration.md (72d0e7f9...), walls-and-retention.md (168ee022...) equal the r3 manifest entries. (1) Skill-prescribed grep, case-insensitive, over instruction.md and all three /instructions notes for judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel|grader|grade|verif|probe|gate|polish|visual|functional|constraint|render|oracle|test.sh|restart_mcp|app_context|harbor|pass|fail returned a single hit: walls-and-retention.md:3 'Everyone signs in with `password123`.' (substring 'pass' in a demo password the profile expects; not machinery). No dimension names, weights, test paths, judge or model names appear. (2) Probe sentinels: the graders use JUDGE-* literals (JUDGE-H1, JUDGE-E1, 'Gate check JUDGE-G1', 'Wall check JUDGE-W0', etc.); none appears in the brief, the notes, or environment/assets/seed_data.json (grep for judge|probe|sentinel|rubric in the seed returned nothing). (3) Criterion ids: the 27 id/name lines (e.g. server_backed_local_application, authenticated_render, wall_every_route, sent_once_in_order, live_updates_keep_my_work) do not appear; the agent-visible text contains no snake_case tokens other than DB_PATH, NODE_PATH and seed_data.json (runtime contract). (4) Verbatim overlap: a token n-gram comparison of brief+notes against every tests/*/*/{judge.toml,prompt.md} and tests/app_context.md found no 10-gram overlap except the account table (walls-and-retention.md:5-11 copied into app_context.md, which is the grader repeating the public account contract, not the brief mirroring criteria). At 7 words the only other overlap is 'shows a short preview of the linked message' (conversations.md:17 vs functional judge.toml), a short product phrase, not a leaked criterion. (5) Agent-image Dockerfile copies only instructions/ and assets/; no tests path is exposed. Items such as GET /api/health, port 3000, /app/app.db, DB_PATH, fixed clock and accounts are the runtime contract that row 4 requires, not grader machinery. The closing line instruction.md:9 ('Before you hand it over, please try it the way we'll use it...') is a requester-voice nudge and names no judge, criterion or test. Adversarial checks: a broken app cannot exploit the brief to recognise or special-case grader sentinels because none are disclosed; a conforming app cannot be failed by this row because nothing in the brief directs it at grader internals. This row is a static source property; no runtime measurement is required for it, so no missing-evidence risk applies to this row (runtime evidence for other rows is not assessed here).
